Now I'll view one reference image from Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers to confirm.

The test image shows scattered multi-septate, clavate (club-shaped) conidia with 4-7 transverse septa, olive-green coloration, some in short chains — classic Alternaria conidial morphology. The reference Alternaria image confirms microscopic fungal structures from the same disease category, though it shows conidiophores rather than free conidia. The spore morphology in the test image (multicellular, segmented, elongated, greenish) is definitively consistent with Alternaria species causing black molds/stem cankers on tomato.
